messages:
maria: Quick note — noticed p99 latency spike on A10 dedicated pool during the late-night canary. profiler shows frequent fallback to the generic kernel for attention when batch composition has high seq-length variance.

jin: Seen similar on T4 yesterday. p50 OK, but p99 up ~120ms on mixed-length workloads. KV cache hit rate looked fine; fragmentation / packing seems to be the trigger for kernel selector thresholds.

rob: Do we have exact traces? stack from the profiler (snippet):
```
kernel_selector: chosen=generic-attn reason=packed_fail ragged_ratio=0.43
alloc_log: pack_fragments=0.27 kv_swaps=12
latency_hist: p50=28ms p95=88ms p99=210ms
```

maria: Yep — attaching summary: A10 canary 03:12–04:00 shows ragged_ratio spikes when small prompts are intermixed with long completions. That forces the selector to prefer a fallback kernel with worse per-token throughput.

sandra: My read: two levers — (1) change kernel selector thresholds so slightly higher ragged_ratio still picks the fast kernel if total tokens in batch under a per-GPU token budget, (2) tighten per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch so packed kernel sees more homogeneous packs.

jin: Proposed safe defaults for experiment:
- max_batch_size (seqs): L4=16, T4=12, A10=24, A100=48, H100=64
- max_tokens_per_batch: L4=40_000, T4=30_000, A10=60_000, A100=120_000, H100=140_000

rob: Sounds reasonable. We should also try kernel_selector delta: allow packed-attn up to ragged_ratio=0.55 if tokens_in_batch < token_budget. That should avoid unnecessary fallbacks on short-heavy batches.

maria: Run plan: 1) perf-canary A10 w/ new token_budget + selector change on a single shard, 2) collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, and kernel-usage histogram, 3) compare cost/tokens. I'll run tests tonight. Command I'm using: `./perf_harness.sh --gpu A10 --tag=a10-batch-ceil-0423 --max-tokens 60000 --max-batch 24 --selector-delta 0.12`

perfbot: perfbot: canary queued: a10-batch-ceil-0423, shard=shard-7, start=1745233600

jin: Reminder to capture KV cache fragmentation metric: `kv_frag_ratio` in runtime metrics. If kv_frag_ratio > 0.25 we need to consider warmup packing or prefix caching to reduce swaps.

sandra: If canary looks good, we should roll to a small fleet of A10 + T4, monitor error budget and cost per token. Also add an alert for sudden kernel_fallback_rate > 5% in 5m window.

rob: I'll create the rollout PR and a short runbook for ops: links and commands, and add the perfbot dashboard tile to the canary group.

maria: Thanks — ping me if perfbot shows regressions. If canary fails, revert selector change first, then reduce token budget. :thumbsup:
